claim: A one-line fenced command wrapped onto multiple PDF baselines fails the release contract.
sandbox: Generated one-page PDF with one source line painted as two text runs at y=700 and y=682; assert exit 1, code.flow-changed, and HOLD proof.

claim: Painted text is checked against every media or crop box edge.
sandbox: Generated PDFs place text beyond left, right, top, and bottom MediaBox edges and beyond a non-default CropBox; every case must exit 1.

claim: Missing fenced code is reported as a release defect.
sandbox: Generated PDF omits the fenced source line; assert exit 1 and code.content-missing.

claim: A Markdown fragment cannot pass with the wrong PDF destination.
sandbox: Generated PDF maps the second source fragment to an unrelated destination; assert exit 1 and link.destination-missing.

claim: Missing syntax color warns by default and fails when warnings are denied.
sandbox: Generated PDF has a language-tagged fence and no color operator; assert warning with exit 0, then exit 1 under --deny-warnings.

claim: Linux renderer subprocesses cannot create network connections.
where: README Renderer safety; landing facts and safety
sandbox: Launch a custom curl renderer against a loopback listener and assert the listener receives no connection.

claim: The bundled sample runs without user files or a renderer and writes a HOLD proof.
sandbox: Run codeproof demo into a fresh temporary directory; compare the copied sample and assert generated PDF, code.flow-changed, and proof output.

claim: The documentation demo makes only same-origin requests and stores no tracking data.
sandbox: Fresh browser context runs the sample flow while recording origins, cookies, localStorage, and sessionStorage.

claim: The installed documentation shell works offline after the first visit.
sandbox: Dedicated fresh browser context waits for an active service worker, goes offline, reloads, and asserts the page and offline state.

claim: The package and locked dependencies declare support for Rust 1.88.
sandbox: Read package metadata under --locked and fail if any dependency declares a newer Rust version.
